name: Tophet
overview: Tophet, also known as Topheth, was a place in the valley of the sons of Hinnom where the Israelites committed the abominable practice of passing their children through fire to the pagan god Molech. This horrific idolatry provoked the Lord's anger and was strongly condemned in Scripture, as seen in Jeremiah's denunciation of the high places of Tophet and the promise of its destruction. King Josiah later defiled Tophet to prevent this evil, highlighting God's judgment against such sacrifices and idolatry. Isaiah portrays Tophet as a place of fiery judgment, prepared by God as a symbol of divine wrath.
